title: Fast Radio Burst Progenitors
bottleneck: Fast radio bursts release millisecond bursts of enormous energy, with some repeating and most appearing once; magnetar flares explain some repeaters, but the one-off population's origin is unknown. Host-galaxy diversity (from star-forming dwarfs to quiescent ellipticals) resists a single-progenitor model. Some bursts show complex time-frequency structure suggesting magnetospheric emission, while others look like far-away shock masers.
why_it_blocks: FRBs could become cosmological probes (baryon census, magnetic fields) once their engines are understood; until then they are an unsolved astrophysical mystery. Until progenitors are known, FRBs cannot be fully trusted as cosmological probes despite their promise.
current_state: CHIME catalogs thousands of FRBs; a Galactic magnetar FRB confirmed one channel, but the dominant cosmological population is unidentified. Localizing hundreds of FRBs to host galaxies is underway and should reveal whether multiple progenitor channels operate.
